literal: To an intoxicated man reason showing, under water to a submerged man fire having searched like that.
translation: Trying to reason with a drunkard is like searching with a torch for a man who has sunk underwater.
modern: குடிபோதையில் இருப்பவனுக்கு நியாயங்களை எடுத்துக் கூறுவது, தண்ணீருக்கு அடியில் மூழ்கியவனைத் தீப்பந்தம் கொண்டு தேடுவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a striking simile to illustrate the futility of arguing with someone who is drunk. The word 'களித்தானை' refers to an intoxicated person whose mind is completely clouded. Trying to show them 'காரணம்' (reason or logic) is compared to searching for someone who has submerged 'கீழ் நீர்' (under water) using 'தீ' (fire or a torch). Just as a torch is extinguished underwater and cannot illuminate the depths, logic and reason cannot penetrate a mind submerged in intoxication.
